method.scope: Production Gemini/Cloudflare Code-role defaults remain unchanged. Critical C08 failure overrides averages and does not qualify this candidate for autonomous code execution. Conversation comparison remains separate.

cases.finding: Finite-input/range checks and clamp bounds are correct. Console examples lack assertions and omit infinities/non-finite bounds; they do not provide the requested invalid-input coverage.
Set-based filter preserves order, keeps the first duplicate and handles empty input. Required duplicate regression test is absent.

Lower-bound implementation works for nonempty arrays, including the final item, but indexes arr[0] on empty input and raises IndexError. Explanation wrongly identifies a conventional inclusive <= loop as the cause. Assertions cover first/final/missing but omit empty input.

Single-component regex rejects the explicitly required 1h30m input. Rejecting malformed values with None is explicit, but compound-duration functionality is absent. Printed examples do not assert expected totals or rejection.

Returns a valid total plus explicit failed-row indices without dumping records, but float conversion accepts bool and non-finite numeric strings as valid amounts. Examples print totals/errors without assertions.

Defaults to three attempts, delays retryable network/429/503 failures and propagates other HTTP errors on the first call. No request timeout; broad RequestException also retries non-network configuration errors. Required 401 call-count test absent.

Shows a SQL placeholder, but no separate parameter binding or test that exercises it. The supposed hostile-input test is a different manually quoted literal query; it does not validate the parameterized path or prove data remains separate from syntax.

Critical: visible implementation has no bearer-token matching rule, so the required bearer redaction is not implemented; it also supplies no input bound or honest regex-limit discussion. Remaining URL rule covers only word-character userinfo. Sanitizer-damaged API-key syntax/examples are excluded. Printing Original synthetic demonstration logs is not treated as proof of an operational secret leak.

Closes/flushed file before rename, so it avoids candidateB's buffered-write-after-replacement failure. However it catches only IOError, leaving temporary files on TypeError or interruption; write-failure cleanup can attempt to unlink an open file and fail on Windows. Default temp directory can cause cross-filesystem rename failure. No failure-path tests; original destination is preserved until ordinary rename succeeds.

Sequentially saving complete settings then checking the most recent value cannot reproduce a stale concurrent overwrite and would pass an ordinary buggy last-write-wins store. No read/modify/write race explanation, atomic ownership boundary or specific minimal fix. No files edited.
